### Western New England Bancorp, Inc. Reports Results for Three and Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 and Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend


October 27, 2026


THE COMPANY ALSO ANNOUNCES A NEW 5% SHARE REPURCHASE PLAN


WESTFIELD, Mass., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Western New England Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company” or “WNEB”) (NasdaqGS: WNEB), the holding company for Westfield Bank (the “Bank”), announced today the unaudited results of operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $6.3 million, or $0.32 per diluted share, compared to net income of $3.2 million, or $0.16 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. On a linked quarter basis, net income was $6.3 million, or $0.32 per diluted share, as compared to net income of $3.6 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income was $14.7 million, or $0.74 per diluted share, compared to net income of $10.1 million, or $0.50 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.


The Company also announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.07 per share on the Company’s common stock. The dividend will be payable on or about November 25, 2026 to shareholders of record on November 11, 2026.


In addition, the Company announced that today its Board of Directors authorized a new stock repurchase plan (the “2026 Plan”), pursuant to which the Company may repurchase up to 1.0 million shares of the Company’s common stock, or approximately 5.0% of the Company’s outstanding common stock as of today. The 2026 Plan will commence upon the completion of the Company’s existing stock repurchase plan (the “2025 Plan”). The 2025 Plan was approved by the Board of Directors on April 22, 2025. At September 30, 2026, there were 276,465 shares of common stock available for repurchase under the 2025 Plan.


James C. Hagan, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented, “I am pleased to report the results for the third quarter of 2026. Our diversified loans and deposits, along with our disciplined approach to managing funding costs, resulted in an increase in the net interest margin to 3.07%. At September 30, 2026, core deposits and non-interest-bearing deposits represented 69.8% and 25.3% of total deposits, respectively, while the average cost of deposits stood at 1.73% for the three months ended September 30, 2026.


We continue to focus on extending credit within our markets and servicing the needs of our existing customer base while ensuring new opportunities present the appropriate risk-adjusted return. Consistent with our prudent credit culture, we continue to proactively identify and manage credit risk within the loan portfolio. At September 30, 2026, our asset quality remained strong, with total delinquency at 0.41% of total loans, and total nonaccrual loans at 0.36% of total loans.


We remain disciplined in our capital management strategies. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased 596,000 shares of common stock and have 276,465 shares of common stock available for repurchase under the 2025 Plan.”


Hagan concluded, “Today, we announced the 2026 Plan, which will commence upon the completion of the 2025 Plan. We continue to believe that repurchasing shares represents a valuable use of the Company’s capital and is an integral element of our capital management strategies. We are pleased to be able to continue to return value to shareholders through share repurchases and quarterly cash dividends. Our commitment to strong capital and strong liquidity levels gives us a solid foundation to take advantage of opportunities in the markets we serve and to enhance shareholder value in the long term.”


**Key Highlights:**


**Loans and Deposits**


At September 30, 2026, total loans increased $11.1 million, or 0.5%, from $2.2 billion, or 79.7% of total assets, at December 31, 2025, to $2.2 billion, or 79.8% of total assets. The increase was primarily driven by an increase in residential real estate loans, including home equity loans, of $57.3 million, or 6.7%, partially offset by a decrease in commercial real estate loans of $40.6 million, or 3.7%, and a decrease in commercial and industrial loans of $4.9 million, or 2.2%. At September 30, 2026, total deposits of $2.4 billion increased $67.2 million, or 2.8%, from December 31, 2025, primarily due to an increase in time deposits of $42.2 million, or 6.1%, and an increase in core deposits of $25.0 million, or 1.5%.


**Allowance for Credit Losses and Credit Quality**


At September 30, 2026, the allowance for credit losses was $19.6 million, or 0.89% of total loans, compared to $20.3 million, or 0.93% of total loans, at December 31, 2025. The allowance for credit losses, as a percentage of nonaccrual loans, was 248.4% and 393.2% at September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, respectively. At September 30, 2026, nonaccrual loans totaled $7.9 million, or 0.36% of total loans, compared to $5.2 million, or 0.24% of total loans, at December 31, 2025. Total delinquent loans increased from $3.1 million, or 0.14% of total loans, at December 31, 2025, to $9.1 million, or 0.41% of total loans, at September 30, 2026. Of the $9.1 million in past due loans, 74.1% are residential real estate loans. At September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, the Company did not have any other real estate owned.


**Net Interest Margin**


The net interest margin increased seven basis points from 3.00% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 to 3.07% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The net interest margin, on a tax-equivalent basis (a non-GAAP financial measure), increased seven basis points from 3.02% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to 3.09% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. See pages 20-22 for the related net interest margin calculations and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures.


**Stock Repurchase Program**


On April 22, 2025, the Board of Directors authorized the 2025 Plan, pursuant to which the Company may repurchase up to 1.0 million shares of its common stock, or approximately 4.8%, of the Company’s then-outstanding shares of common stock. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 215,000 shares of its common stock at an average price per share of $13.85. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 596,000 shares of its common stock at an average price per share of $13.72. At September 30, 2026, there were 276,465 shares of common stock available for repurchase under the 2025 Plan.


Today the Board of Directors authorized the 2026 Plan, pursuant to which the Company may repurchase up to 1.0 million shares of common stock, or approximately 5.0% of the Company’s outstanding shares as of today the date the 2026 Plan was announced. Repurchases under the 2026 Plan will commence upon the completion of the 2025 Plan.


The repurchase of shares under the Company’s stock repurchase plans is administered through an independent broker. The shares of common stock repurchased under both the 2025 Plan and the 2026 Plan have been and will continue to be, as applicable, purchased from time to time at prevailing market prices, through open market or privately negotiated transactions, or otherwise, depending upon market conditions. There is no guarantee as to the exact number, or value, of shares that will be repurchased by the Company, and the Company may discontinue repurchases at any time that the Company’s management (“Management”) determines additional repurchases are not warranted. The timing and amount of additional share repurchases under both the 2025 Plan and the 2026 Plan will depend on a number of factors, including the Company’s stock price performance, ongoing capital planning considerations, general market conditions, and applicable legal requirements.


**Book Value and Tangible Book Value**


The Company’s book value per share was $12.34 at September 30, 2026, compared to $12.16 at December 31, 2025, while tangible book value per share, a non-GAAP financial measure, increased $0.18, or 1.6%, from $11.49 at December 31, 2025, to $11.67 at September 30, 2026. See pages 20-22 for the related tangible book value calculation and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures.


**Net Income for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to the Three Months Ended June 30, 2026**


For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $6.3 million, or $0.32 per diluted share, compared to $3.6 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, for the three months ended June 30, 2026. Net interest income increased $673,000, or 3.5%, the provision for credit losses decreased $2.5 million, non-interest income increased $512,000, or 15.1%, and non-interest expense increased $158,000, or 1.0%. Return on average assets and return on average equity were 0.91% and 10.1%, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.53% and 5.84%, respectively, for the three months ended June 30, 2026.


**Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin**


Net interest income, our primary driver of revenues, increased $673,000, or 3.5%, from $19.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to $20.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The increase in net interest income was due to an increase in interest and dividend income of $522,000, or 1.7%, and a decrease in interest expense of $151,000, or 1.3%.


During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the net interest margin was 3.07%, compared to 3.00% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The net interest margin, on a tax-equivalent basis (a non-GAAP financial measure), was 3.09% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 3.02% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The average yield on interest-earning assets, without the impact of tax-equivalent adjustments, increased four basis points from 4.77% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to 4.81% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The average loan yield, without the impact of tax-equivalent adjustments, increased four basis points from 5.12% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to 5.16% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. See pages 20-22 for the related net interest margin calculations and a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures.


For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the average cost of core deposits, which the Company defines as all deposits except time deposits, was 1.01% compared to 1.03% for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The average cost of time deposits decreased one basis point from 3.38% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to 3.37% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The average cost of borrowings, including subordinated debt, increased 71 basis points from 5.15% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to 5.86% for the three months ended September 30, 2026. During the same period, average borrowings decreased $32.6 million, or 37.9%. Average demand deposits, an interest-free source of funds, increased $15.3 million, or 2.6%, from $593.1 million, or 24.9% of total average deposits, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to $608.4 million, or 25.2% of total average deposits, for the three months ended September 30, 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the average cost of total funds, including non-interest-bearing accounts and borrowings, decreased four basis points to 1.82%.


**Provision for (Reversal of) Credit Losses**


The Company recorded a reversal of credit losses of $971,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a provision for credit losses of $1.6 million during the three months ended June 30, 2026. The decrease of $2.5 million in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was determined by a number of factors, including a decrease in net charge-offs, paydowns in the loan portfolio, changes in the loan portfolio mix, and Management’s consideration of existing economic conditions, including a slight improvement in the quarterly economic outlook from the Federal Reserve Bank. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses included a partial charge-off of $1.8 million on a non-owner occupied commercial real estate participation loan relationship (“participation loan”) secured by an office building. In June 2026, the Company was notified by the lead bank of the participation loan that on June 4, 2026, the borrower filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy (“Bankruptcy Filing”). Immediately prior to notification of the Bankruptcy Filing, the Company’s 40% portion of the participation loan had a carrying value of $3.4 million and the borrower was then current with its scheduled payments. At September 30, 2026, the relationship was past due and is included in nonaccrual loans. Management continues to monitor macroeconomic variables related to increasing interest rates, tariffs, increased energy costs, inflation and concerns of an economic downturn, and believes it is appropriately reserved for the current economic environment.


During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded net recoveries of $274,000, or 0.05% of average loans, on an annualized basis, compared to net charge-offs of $1.8 million, or 0.33% of average loans, on an annualized basis, for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The net charge-offs recorded during the three months ended June 30, 2026, were attributable to the $1.8 million charge-off of the participation loan discussed above.


**Non-Interest Income**


For the three months ended September 30, 2026, non-interest income was $3.9 million, an increase of $512,000, or 15.1%, from the three months ended June 30, 2026. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported the sale of two buildings located at 219 and 229 Exchange Street, Chicopee, Massachusetts to the City of Chicopee. The transaction resulted in a total gross cash consideration of $2.4 million and a gain of $712,000 on the sale. Excluding the gain, non-interest income decreased $200,000, or 5.9%. Service charges and fees on deposits decreased $157,000, or 6.5%, from $2.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, to $2.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, service charges and fees on deposits included annual VISA incentives due to increased transaction volumes.


Income from bank-owned life insurance (“BOLI”) decreased $19,000, or 3.6%, from the three months ended June 30, 2026, to $516,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported unrealized losses on marketable equity securities of $2,000, compared to unrealized gains of $47,000 during the three months ended June 30, 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, and the three months ended June 30, 2026, wealth management income totaled $382,000 and $389,000, respectively. During the same period, assets under management increased from $256.6 million at June 30, 2026, to $261.4 million at September 30, 2026, reflecting net investment appreciation and assets acquired.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, non-interest expense increased $158,000, or 1.0%, to $16.5 million from the three months ended June 30, 2026. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, salaries and employee benefits expense increased $128,000, or 1.4%, primarily due to one additional day of payroll expense. Debit card processing and ATM network costs increased $70,000, or 10.9%, furniture and equipment expense increased $29,000, or 7.2%, data processing expense increased $12,000, or 1.2%, FDIC insurance expense increased $4,000, or 1.1%, and other non-interest expense increased $43,000, or 3.1%. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in professional fees of $82,000, or 13.2%, a decrease in software-related expenses of $42,000, or 5.9%, and a decrease in advertising expense of $5,000, or 1.1%.


For the three months ended September 30, 2026, and the three months ended June 30, 2026, the efficiency ratio was 69.1% and 72.0%, respectively. The decrease in the efficiency ratio was driven by an increase in total revenues, defined as the sum of net interest income and non-interest income, of $1.2 million, or 5.2%, during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended June 30, 2026.


**Income Tax Provision**


Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $2.1 million, with an effective tax rate of 24.6%, compared to $1.2 million, with an effective tax rate of 25.1%, for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The increase is due to higher projected pre-tax income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2026.

The securities, with the exception of $15.4 million in corporate bonds, are issued by the United States government or government-sponsored enterprises and are therefore either explicitly or implicitly guaranteed as to the timely payment of contractual principal and interest. These positions are deemed to have no credit impairment, therefore, the disclosed unrealized losses within the securities portfolio relate primarily to changes in prevailing interest rates. Absent credit deterioration or other adverse factors, unrealized losses attributable to interest-rate movements would generally be expected to diminish as the securities approach maturity.


Management regularly reviews the portfolio for securities in an unrealized loss position. At September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, the Company did not record any credit impairment charges on its securities portfolio and attributed the unrealized losses primarily due to fluctuations in general interest rates or changes in expected prepayments and not due to credit quality. The primary objective of the Company’s investment portfolio is to provide liquidity and to secure municipal deposit accounts while preserving the safety of principal. The available-for-sale and held-to-maturity portfolios are both eligible for pledging to the Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) and Federal Reserve Bank (“FRB”) as collateral for borrowings.
